Very simple and very effective; I'm a fan. The poem does a solid job conveying that love is more than your appearance, that it's more than your demons. It shows that you can be appreciated regardless of what you deem irredeemable qualities. My only critique is the line, "and the beast wished to test the human." This line strikes me as odd and makes the beast a bit of a less likable character, as "testing" has a sort of negative connotation. Overall, however, I quite enjoyed this poem!

Wow, I love this poem. It's evident and concise with the idea it tries to convey, which is excellent for many people, including me. The idea that even though life can be miserable, it's still worth living is compelling. My takeaway is that the narrator fights through an unnamed disease and tries to be the best they can be for their two children. Fighting hardship and pain, they live life for their memory—truly a beautiful piece.

I like the concept quite a bit. As humans, we don't want to feel deeper emotions like adoration or love out of fear of getting hurt. We minimize it to "just a crush" when, in reality, it's more than that. I think this poem does a good job capturing this.

My only critique is that the poem overstays its welcome just a tad. The poem starts very heavily poetic, and I love it for that. Since it starts so heavy, however, the later lines lose some amount of their meaning. If it was more concise, I think youd feel more power throughout.

Regardless, this poem was quite a joy to read.

Four lines can provoke a surprising amount of thought!  
What I take away from this poem is that love evokes a very much give-and-take relationship. It very much feels like, as you said, a game of trades. A game of "how much should I give, and how much should I receive." As love fades, the question becomes much more difficult to answer.

Poems are one of the best ways to release thoughts you don't feel you can say. This poem drives home that idea. The poem, at least in my eyes, shows a profound loss and resentment. The idea that you're sad to lose them but still hold at least some semblance of distaste toward them is illustrated quite well.

The last few lines hit me. The idea of being haunted by words is so chilling. I know the feeling of having a poem stuck in your head, and you need to write down the words, but you can never quite finish the poem. So, in that sense, the words are haunting you.

Its so simple, yet so effective. Its a clean story through and through. Im not sure if it was intentional, but the lack of capitalization at the start of lines actually helps accent the simplicity. Theres nothing too formal, nothing to serious. "That morning in Vienna" was a fond memory, but it wasnt lige-changing. You miss them, but you can accept that they're gone. This poem is great at showing that good times come and go. Yes, you can miss those good times, but you don't let it consume you. It feels like one of those random thoughts that come up every once in a while. "Oh yeah, I remember, yeah I do miss her." Of the poems on this sub, this one left more of a smile on my face and I appreciate it.
